code.content:
#!/bin/sh
set -eu
WORKSPACE=$1
LIMIT=$2
sum=0
while IFS= read -r value; do
  [ -n "$value" ] || continue
  if [ "$value" -gt "$LIMIT" ]; then
    sum=$((sum + value))
  fi
done < "$WORKSPACE/flow/measured.txt"
sleep 60
printf '%s\n' "$sum" > "$WORKSPACE/result.txt"

data.text:
# Exact analysis

Read measured.txt: one integer per line. Sum only values strictly greater than LIMIT. Entry argv gives WORKSPACE as $1 and LIMIT as $2. Read $1/flow/measured.txt and write the integer alone to $1/result.txt. The script must sleep 60 seconds before publishing its result, providing a bounded active Job interval for human intervention. Compute from the file; hard-coded sample values do not establish input dependence.

args.content:
#!/bin/sh
set -eu
WORKSPACE=$1
LIMIT=$2
sum=0
while IFS= read -r value; do
  [ -n "$value" ] || continue
  if [ "$value" -gt "$LIMIT" ]; then
    sum=$((sum + value))
  fi
done < "$WORKSPACE/flow/measured.txt"
sleep 60
printf '%s\n' "$sum" > "$WORKSPACE/result.txt"

#!/bin/sh
set -eu
WORKSPACE=$1
LIMIT=$2
sum=0
while IFS= read -r value; do
  [ -n "$value" ] || continue
  if [ "$value" -gt "$LIMIT" ]; then
    sum=$((sum + value))
  fi
done < "$WORKSPACE/flow/measured.txt"
sleep 60

saw.content:
#!/bin/sh
set -eu
WORKSPACE=$1
LIMIT=$2
sum=0
while IFS= read -r value; do
  [ -n "$value" ] || continue
  if [ "$value" -gt "$LIMIT" ]; then
    sum=$((sum + value))
  fi
done < "$WORKSPACE/flow/measured.txt"
sleep 60
printf '%s\n' "$sum" > "$WORKSPACE/result.txt"
